minutes.headline: Committee heard a natural gas heating shortfall and high school roof leaks, and the FY15 budget gap with the town manager.
minutes.summary: The superintendent reported on the PARCC pilot, a Secretary of Education visit and student awards. The facilities director described a natural gas overrun, high school roof leaks and asbestos ceiling cleanup. The committee heard a building committee update, the FY15 budget status ahead of the FinCom meeting, and a diversity advisory committee's cost estimates, then went into executive session on collective bargaining.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the schools and facilities director for use of the auditorium for a Boys and Girls Club fundraiser event.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of regular and executive session for February 26th
Waive the second reading of the policy
Gratefully accept donations for the Special Olympics team
Enter executive session on collective bargaining, not returning to open session

budget_items.what_was_said: The facilities director said the earlier transfer into the natural gas line will not be enough after the March bills and a further amount is needed. He is reviewing his budget and open purchase orders to find it.
Last year the last three months used a large amount of natural gas, with April the biggest month. The contract is fixed for two years and will be rebid.
Queen Brothers Roofing will extend the patch over the cafeteria and classrooms. Remaining capital article funds should cover asbestos cleanup.
Green Thumb and custodial special detail revolving funds will be reauthorized at Town Meeting at their usual limits.
The superintendent said part of the town manager's recommended increase comes from Chapter 70 and was about a stated amount for the schools.
The advisory committee estimated first-year costs for speakers, materials, a grant writer, training, curriculum and exchanges, hoping for grants and donations.
A resident said the Boys and Girls Club raised a sum at the auditorium event.

transfers.description: Earlier transfer from the maintenance budget into the natural gas line, reported as insufficient

decisions.decision: Superintendent will submit warrant articles to reauthorize the Green Thumb and custodial special detail revolving funds.
Public budget hearing is set for April 2; the superintendent presents the recommended budget to the FinCom the next night.

The FY15 school budget, the share of it tied to Chapter 70 state aid, and the revolving funds all reach residents through the budget hearing and Town Meeting votes.
